relationships.subject: painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy
relationships.evidence_quote: epidermal keratinocyte immunoreactivity for Nav1.6, Nav1.7, and CGRP were all significantly elevated among the PDPN cohort compared with control

relationships.subject: topical 5% lidocaine
relationships.evidence_quote: the increased levels of keratinocyte Nav1.6, Nav1.7, and CGRP immunoreactivity in PDPN patients were all significantly reduced to approximate control levels following topical 5% lidocaine treatment

relationships.subject: Nav1.7
relationships.evidence_quote: the pre-treatment keratinocyte biomarkers Nav1.7 and CGRP were also statistically significant predictors of responder status

key_findings: Keratinocyte Nav1.6, Nav1.7 and CGRP are elevated in painful DPN (not low-pain DPN) and normalised after 4-week topical lidocaine; pretreatment levels predict responders.
Epidermal and dermal innervation loss was comparable in painful and low-pain DPN, so innervation loss alone does not explain pain.
